:::{#def-lebesgue-measure}
#### Lebesgue measure

**Lebesgue measure** on $\reals$
is the [measure](#def-measure) $\lambda$
on the [Borel $\sigma$-algebra](#def-borel-sigma-algebra) $\borel$
that assigns each [interval](sets-functions.qmd#def-interval) its length:
for real numbers $a \le b$,

$$\lambda([a, b]) = \lambda((a, b)) = \lambda([a, b)) = \lambda((a, b]) \eqdef b - a,$$

and $\lambda(I) \eqdef \infty$ for each unbounded interval $I$.

**Lebesgue measure on an interval** $I$, such as $[0, 1]$,
is $\lambda$ applied only to the Borel sets that are subsets of $I$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-lebesgue-measure-exists}
#### Lebesgue measure exists

Exactly one measure on $\borel$ assigns every interval its length;
constructing it takes more measure theory than these notes cover
(see [Wikipedia: Lebesgue measure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebesgue_measure),
which also extends $\lambda$ to a larger $\sigma$-algebra,
the Lebesgue-measurable sets, with the same values on Borel sets).

:::
